newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian wants Jospin to delay Vilvoorde close.
newsitem.headline: Belgian wants Jospin to delay Vilvoorde close.

text.p: Louis Tobback, president of the Flemish Socialist Party SP, has urged French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to delay the closure of the Belgian Renault plant and start discussions about alternatives for a shut-down, the SP said in a statement.
It said Tobback and Jospin had discussed the issue for a considerable time in Malmo, Sweden, at the European Social Democratic Parties' Congress.
Tobback told Jospin he was willing to travel to Paris this weekend to explain the alternative proposals and urged Jospin to meet Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene soon, the SP said.
Tobback said Jospin had not made any concrete commitments but "gave the impression he was taking the Renault dossier very seriously", the statement said.
Jospin said last week, before Sunday's parliamentary elections which he won, that he would ask Renault to study alternatives to allow the plant to remain open.
Renault, which announced the closure with 3,100 job losses in February, reiterated on Wednesday it was indispensable to cut costs and streamline its European car assembly operations.
The French Socialist Party said on Wednesday it opposed the plan by Renault to close the assembly plant in Vilvoorde.
Renault lost 5.25 billion francs ($901.2 million) last year and is struggling to break even this year.
